channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: The Most Important Opinions, January-December 2025
item.description: Summaries of the most significant Massachusetts federal and state court decisions issued in 2025.

item.title: Consumer class action accuses Red Sox of ‘drip pricing’
item.description: A consumer class action alleges the Boston Red Sox used drip pricing and junk fees to hide ticket costs, violating Massachusetts and Rhode Island consumer laws.

item.title: U.S. Supreme Court asked to review Massachusetts plumbing license law
item.description: A Massachusetts homeowner asks the Supreme Court to review a plumbing license law, raising constitutional questions about rational basis review and property rights.

item.title: Attorney general suing 9 towns over zoning law compliance
item.description: Attorney General Andrea J. Campbell is suing nine Massachusetts communities in an attempt to get the towns to comply with a 2021 law intended to boost housing production near MBTA stations.

item.title: Healey targets ICE, immigrant protections with executive order, bill
item.description: Gov. Maura Healey signed an executive order limiting ICE enforcement, banning 287(g) agreements and protecting courts, schools, and hospitals.

item.title: Bank of America must face Epstein trafficking lawsuit
item.description: A federal judge ruled Bank of America must face claims it knowingly benefited from Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking, while dismissing a case against BNY Mellon.

item.title: 7 things I’ve done in the last 5 years that catapulted my career
item.description: Over the past five years, I’ve implemented seven strategies that meaningfully moved the needle in my legal career. Each required time, effort, and in some cases financial investment.

item.title: The challenge of corruption
item.description: Over time, it became known that you had to “pay to play” in Brockton. To get work from the DPW, you had to pay Frank Wallen. As an assistant U.S. attorney in Boston in the U.S. Attorney’s Office Public Corruption Unit, I was assigned to the case.

item.title: Veteran suffers recurrence of PTSD in wake of car accident
item.description: The case involved a motor vehicle accident in September 2024. The defendant, driving a commercial motor vehicle, rear-ended the plaintiff, causing back and neck injuries.

item.title: Delayed post-surgery treatment blamed for cognitive decline
item.description: The plaintiff underwent bariatric surgery without any complications. Over the next 54 days, the plaintiff had four hospital admissions and spent 20 days as an inpatient.
